name: Díl
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Díl was an obscure Irish heroine. The Book of Invasions is the only surviving source that mentions her. That text names her as the wife of Donn, a figure as shadowy as she was. She drowned as her people, the Milesians, arrived in Ireland. The Milesians were the final group thought to have settled the island. Díl's death came at the moment of their landing, as recorded in that single account. Scholars know little else about her. Transmission of Irish legend kept only her name, her marriage, and the manner of her end. Her place rests on one brief entry within a larger genealogical compilation.

okr.objective: Record the single known account of the Irish heroine Díl as wife of Donn who drowned on the Milesians' arrival.
key_results: The Book of Invasions is the only source that names Díl.
She was the wife of the mysterious figure Donn.
She drowned as the Milesians arrived in Ireland.
Scholars know no other details about her.
